items.stem: Explain why (x − 5)(x − 9) = 3 cannot be solved by writing x − 5 = 3 or x − 9 = 3.
items.answer: The null factor law only applies to a product equal to 0; many pairs of factors multiply to a non-zero number.
items.markingKey: The null factor law only applies to a product equal to 0; many pairs of factors multiply to a non-zero number. (R1 A1)

items.answer: x = −3 also works: x² − 9 = (x − 3)(x + 3) = 0, so x = ±3.

items.stem: The width w of a rectangle satisfies w² + 4w − 140 = 0, giving w = 10 or w = -14. Explain which value is valid and why.
items.markingKey: A width must be positive, so w = −14 is rejected (R1); w = 10 (A1).

items.stem: Briefly explain why, if (x − 3)(x + 5) = 0, then x = 3 or x = −5.
items.answer: If a product of two numbers is zero, at least one of them must be zero (null factor law), so x − 3 = 0 or x + 5 = 0.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: If a product of two numbers is zero, at least one of them must be zero (null factor law), so x − 3 = 0 or x + 5 = 0. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Without solving, explain why 1x² + 1 = 0 has no real solutions, and confirm using the discriminant.
Elena writes: "(x − 3)² = 5 gives x = 3 + √5 only." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Square roots give ±: x − 3 = ±√5, so x = 3 ± √5.
items.markingKey: Square roots give ±: x − 3 = ±√5, so x = 3 ± √5. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why you must check solutions of a quadratic word problem against the context.
items.answer: The algebra may give values that are mathematically correct but impossible in context, e.g. a negative length or time.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The algebra may give values that are mathematically correct but impossible in context, e.g. a negative length or time. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Aiko solves x² = 9x by dividing both sides by x and gets x = 9. Explain what has gone wrong.
items.answer: Dividing by x loses x = 0. Rearranging: x² − 9x = 0, x(x − 9) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 9.
items.markingKey: Dividing by x loses x = 0. Rearranging: x² − 9x = 0, x(x − 9) = 0, so x = 0 or x = 9. (R1 A1)
